title: A mule on 7 complaints: full freeze, justified
summary: A 74-day-old current account on the suspect registry, linked to 7 complaints, passes 98% of its money through; LienLine justifies a full freeze and still liens a kirana store only ₹640.

complaint.narrative: A 'part-time job' on Telegram paid small amounts for liking videos, then asked for deposits to unlock earnings. I paid Rs 2,00,000 (UTR 626202252064) and Rs 1,20,000 (UTR 626122913744) by IMPS to Om Sai Enterprises, account XXXX7649, Sahyadri Bank.

grievances.text: Om Sai Enterprises is a genuine trading firm. The freeze of our whole current account is illegal after the High Court judgments; release everything above the disputed amount.

reasons.text: The victim's money arrived via T4 (₹2,00,000.00 of ₹2,00,000.00 from A1), T9 (₹1,20,000.00 of ₹1,20,000.00 from A1). The balance fell to ₹3,200.00 after T13, which caps what can still be traced: ₹3,200.00 under LIBR (lowest intermediate balance).

Full freeze justified by 5 mule signals: On the I4C suspect registry; 7 linked NCRP complaints; Account opened 74 days ago; 98% of available funds passed straight through; Half of T1 moved on within 8 minutes. The amount traceable from this complaint alone is ₹3,200.00 under LIBR; the whole balance is held because of these signals, not this complaint's amount.

Other tracing rules give FIFO ₹0.00, LIFO ₹0.00, PRO_RATA ₹377.17. LIBR is used because it is the accepted standard for mixed funds: it never counts the holder's later, clean credits as the victim's money.

The victim's money arrived via T5 (₹1,87,800.00 of ₹1,96,000.00 from A2). The balance fell to ₹1,460.00 after T15, which caps what can still be traced: ₹1,460.00 under LIBR (lowest intermediate balance).

Mule signals present (Account opened 140 days ago; 100% of available funds passed straight through; Half of T2 moved on within 25 minutes), but no registry hit and fewer than 3 linked complaints, so a full freeze is not justified.

Other tracing rules give FIFO ₹1,398.93, LIFO ₹0.00, PRO_RATA ₹1,360.18. LIBR is used because it is the accepted standard for mixed funds: it never counts the holder's later, clean credits as the victim's money.
₹640.00 of the victim's money is identifiable here under LIBR: it arrived via T15 (₹640.00 of ₹640.00 from A3), and the balance never fell below it afterwards.

The current hold of ₹84,640.00 covers the whole balance. MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026 and Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026 limit a hold to the identifiable disputed amount, so ₹84,000.00 is released.

Other tracing rules give FIFO ₹613.22, LIFO ₹0.00, PRO_RATA ₹596.23. LIBR is used because it is the accepted standard for mixed funds: it never counts the holder's later, clean credits as the victim's money.

letters.subject: Justification for Full Balance Freeze on Account XXXX7649 due to Cyber Fraud Complaint
letters.body:
This letter serves to justify the decision to maintain a full freeze on the balance of ₹19,200.00 in Account XXXX7649, held by Om Sai Enterprises, Sahyadri Bank.

This action is taken following the NCRP acknowledgement 31509260099001 and the notice under Section 106 BNSS dated 22 Sep 2026 from SI M. Rao, Cyber Crime PS, Hyderabad.

Despite traceable credits, such as ₹2,00,000.00 via UTR 626202252064 and ₹1,20,000.00 via UTR 626122913744, the account exhibits significant mule signals. These include listing on the I4C suspect registry, 7 linked NCRP complaints, account opening only 74 days ago, 98% of available funds passing straight through, and half of T1 moving within 8 minutes.

While legal precedents like MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026, and Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026, suggest limiting holds to identifiable disputed amounts, the pervasive mule activity necessitates a full freeze to prevent further illicit movement. The amount traceable to this complaint alone under LIBR is ₹3,200.00.

Decision: Keep the full freeze of the balance of ₹19,200.00.

Nodal Officer, Sahyadri Bank

letters.subject: Reply to Grievance Regarding Hold on Account XXXX7649
letters.body:
This is in reference to your grievance received on 25 Sep 2026 concerning the hold placed on your account, XXXX7649, held with Sahyadri Bank.

We acknowledge the NCRP acknowledgement 31509260099001 and the notice under Section 106 BNSS dated 22 Sep 2026 from SI M. Rao, Cyber Crime PS, Hyderabad.

Our review, considering mule signals such as the account being on the I4C suspect registry, 7 linked NCRP complaints, and 98% of available funds passing straight through, indicates a high risk. While we note traceable credits of ₹2,00,000.00 (UTR 626202252064) and ₹1,20,000.00 (UTR 626122913744) under LIBR, the decision is to keep the full freeze of the balance of ₹19,200.00.

As per legal precedents (MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026; Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026), the hold is limited to the identifiable disputed amount. We confirm that ₹3,200.00 is traceable to this complaint alone under LIBR.

Nodal Officer, Sahyadri Bank

letters.subject: Instruction to Replace Whole-Account Freeze with Lien on Account XXXX1053
letters.body:
This letter serves as a formal instruction regarding the hold placed on Account XXXX1053, held by Ravi Teja.

We acknowledge the current hold of ₹1,460.00 on Account XXXX1053, which was placed following the NCRP acknowledgement 31509260099001 and the notice under Section 106 BNSS dated 22 Sep 2026 from SI M. Rao, Cyber Crime PS, Hyderabad.

Based on the legal precedents set by MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026, and Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026, a hold must be limited to the identifiable disputed amount. The decision is to impose a lien of ₹1,460.00, which represents the amount traceable under the lowest intermediate balance rule.

Therefore, you are instructed to replace the whole-account freeze with a lien of ₹1,460.00. No amount should be released from the hold, as the traceable amount under the lien is ₹1,460.00.

Nodal Officer, Konark Small Finance Bank

letters.subject: Instruction to Replace Whole-Account Freeze with Lien on Account XXXX9483
letters.body:
This letter serves as a formal instruction regarding the hold placed on Account XXXX9483, held by Annapurna Kirana Stores, Vindhya Gramin Bank.

We refer to the NCRP acknowledgement 31509260099001 and the notice under Section 106 BNSS dated 22 Sep 2026 from SI M. Rao, Cyber Crime PS, Hyderabad. The current hold is on the whole balance of ₹84,640.00.

Based on the decision derived from MP High Court, Archana v State of MP, 27 Jul 2026, and Rajasthan High Court, Shree Balaji Enterprises v RBI, 20 Aug 2026, a hold must be limited to the identifiable disputed amount. The traceable amount, as per the lowest intermediate balance rule, is ₹640.00, which corresponds to the credit received via UTR 626108141727.

Therefore, you are hereby instructed to replace the whole-account freeze with a lien of ₹640.00 on Account XXXX9483. The remaining amount of ₹84,000.00 must be released immediately from the hold.

Nodal Officer, Vindhya Gramin Bank
